items.t: Han Chinese and Thai patients: screen for HLA-B*1502 whenever possible before starting; if positive, do not start unless there is no other option.

src.q: Before deciding to initiate treatment, patients of Han Chinese and Thai origin should whenever possible be screened for HLA-B*1502
If these individuals test positive, carbamazepine should not be started unless there is no other therapeutic option.

items.t: Women of childbearing potential: should not be used unless the benefit outweighs the risks after considering alternatives; highly effective contraception needed.

src.q: Carbamazepine should not be used in women of childbearing potential unless the benefit is judged to outweigh the risks following careful consideration of alternative suitable treatment options.

items.t: Start 100 to 200 mg once or twice daily; increase slowly to best response, often 800 to 1200 mg daily in divided doses (some need 1600 to 2000 mg). Target total plasma level about 4 to 12 micrograms/mL. Add to other antiepileptics gradually.

src.q: initially 100-200mg once or twice daily is recommended
This may be followed by a slow increase until the best response is obtained, often 800-1200mg daily. In some instances, 1600mg or even 2000mg daily may be necessary.
usually requires total plasma-carbamazepine concentrations of about 4 to 12 micrograms/mL (17 to 50 micromoles/litre)

items.t: Start 200 to 400 mg daily and raise slowly until pain-free (usually 200 mg 3 to 4 times daily). Maximum recommended 1200 mg/day (the same section also says some need 1600 mg). Once in remission reduce to the lowest maintenance dose and try to stop until another attack.

src.q: Slowly raise the initial dosage of 200-400mg daily until freedom from pain is achieved (normally at 200mg 3-4 times daily).
In some instances, doses of 1600mg Tegretol daily may be needed.
Maximum recommended dose is 1200mg/day. When pain relief has been obtained, attempts should be made to gradually discontinue therapy, until another attack occurs.

items.t: Elderly with trigeminal neuralgia: start 100 mg twice daily, raise slowly; maximum 1200 mg/day. All elderly: choose dose with caution (interactions, pharmacokinetics).

src.q: In elderly patients, an initial dose of 100mg twice daily is recommended.
Due to the potential for drug interactions, the dosage of Tegretol should be selected with caution in elderly patients.

items.t: Start 400 mg daily in divided doses, increase gradually until controlled or up to 1600 mg daily. Usual 400 to 600 mg daily in divided doses.

src.q: Initial starting dose of 400mg daily, in divided doses, increasing gradually until symptoms are controlled or a total of 1600mg given in divided doses is reached.
The usual dosage range is 400-600mg daily, given in divided doses.

items.t: Stopping: do not stop abruptly (may precipitate seizures); withdraw gradually.

src.q: Abrupt withdrawal of Tegretol may precipitate seizures, therefore carbamazepine withdrawal should be gradual.

items.t: Epilepsy: usually 10 to 20 mg/kg daily in several divided doses, with gradual increase. 5 to 10 years: 400 to 600 mg daily; 10 to 15 years: 600 to 1000 mg daily; over 15 years: 800 to 1200 mg daily. Maximum: up to 6 years 35 mg/kg/day; 6 to 15 years 1000 mg/day; over 15 years 1200 mg/day. Tablets not recommended for very young children.

src.q: Usual dosage 10-20mg/kg bodyweight daily taken in several divided doses.
Tegretol tablets are not recommended for very young children.
5-10 years: 400 to 600 mg daily
10-15 years: 600 to 1000mg daily
Maximum recommended dose Up to 6 years of age: 35mg/kg/day 6 to15 years of age: 1000mg/day >15 years of age: 1200mg/day.

items.t: Serious skin reactions (SJS/TEN), mostly in the first months; about 10 times higher risk in some Asian countries. items.t: HLA-A*3101 (European descent, Japanese): higher risk of skin reactions including SJS, TEN, DRESS; routine screening not recommended. If known positive, use only after careful benefit-risk consideration (MHRA).

src.q: There are insufficient data supporting a recommendation for HLA-A*3101 screening before starting carbamazepine treatment.

if patients of European descent or Japanese origin are known to be positive for HLA A*3101 they should only receive carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, or eslicarbazepine after careful consideration of the benefits and risks

items.t: Hypersensitivity (including anaphylaxis, angioedema, DRESS, multi-organ reactions): stop immediately. 25 to 30% of patients hypersensitive to carbamazepine may react to oxcarbazepine; cross-hypersensitivity with phenytoin, primidone, phenobarbital possible.

src.q: In general, if signs and symptoms suggestive of hypersensitivity reactions occur, Tegretol should be withdrawn immediately.
Cross-hypersensitivity can occur between carbamazepine and aromatic antiepileptic drugs (e.g. phenytoin, primidone and phenobarbital).

items.t: Blood disorders (agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia; low platelets or white cells): baseline and periodic full blood count. Stop if leucopenia is severe, progressive or symptomatic, or if significant bone marrow depression.

src.q: complete pre-treatment blood counts, including platelets and possibly reticulocytes and serum iron, should be obtained as a baseline, and periodically thereafter
treatment with Tegretol should be discontinued if the patient develops leucopenia which is severe, progressive or accompanied by clinical manifestations

items.t: Liver: LFTs before and periodically, especially with liver disease history and in the elderly. Withdraw immediately if liver dysfunction worsens or acute liver disease. Raised GGT/ALP from enzyme induction alone is not a reason to stop.

src.q: Liver function tests should also be performed before commencing treatment and periodically thereafter, particularly in patients with a history of liver disease and in elderly patients.
The drug should be withdrawn immediately in cases of aggravated liver dysfunction or acute liver disease.
These enhancements of hepatic metabolising capacity are not an indication for the withdrawal of carbamazepine.

items.t: History of cardiac, hepatic or renal damage, haematological reactions to other drugs, or interrupted courses: prescribe only after critical benefit-risk appraisal and under close monitoring. Baseline and periodic urinalysis and BUN recommended.

src.q: Tegretol should be prescribed only after a critical benefit-risk appraisal and under close monitoring in patients with a history of cardiac, hepatic or renal damage
Baseline and periodic complete urinalysis and BUN determinations are recommended.

items.t: Hyponatraemia: with renal conditions causing low sodium or sodium-lowering drugs (e.g. diuretics), check sodium before starting, after about 2 weeks, then monthly for 3 months. Especially in the elderly.

src.q: serum sodium levels should be measured prior to initiating carbamazepine therapy
serum sodium levels should be measured after approximately two weeks and then at monthly intervals for the first three months during therapy, or according to clinical need

items.t: Mixed seizures including absences (typical or atypical): use with caution; may worsen seizures, stop if so.

src.q: Tegretol should be used with caution in patients with mixed seizures which include absences, either typical or atypical.
In case of exacerbation of seizures, Tegretol should be discontinued.

items.t: Suicidal ideation and behaviour (antiepileptic class effect): monitor and advise patients to seek help.

src.q: patients should be monitored for signs of suicidal ideation and behaviours and appropriate treatment should be considered

items.t: Hypothyroidism: thyroid hormone levels may fall (enzyme induction); monitor thyroid function and adjust replacement.

src.q: Carbamazepine may reduce serum concentrations of thyroid hormones through enzyme induction requiring an increase in dose of thyroid replacement therapy in patients with hypothyroidism.

items.t: Mild anticholinergic activity: closely observe patients with raised intraocular pressure or urinary retention. Latent psychosis may be activated; elderly may become confused or agitated.

src.q: patients with increased intraocular pressure and urinary retention should therefore be closely observed during therapy
The possibility of activation of a latent psychosis and, in elderly patients, of confusion or agitation should be borne in mind.

items.t: Falls (ataxia, dizziness, somnolence, hypotension, confusion): reassess fall risk in long-term use. Bone: long-term use linked with reduced bone density and fractures; consider vitamin D for at-risk patients (MHRA).

src.q: complete risk assessment of fall should be considered recurrently for patients on long-term Tegretol treatment
vitamin D supplementation should be considered for at-risk patients who receive long-term treatment with primidone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, or sodium valproate

items.t: Potent CYP3A4 inducer: lowers levels of many co-medications. Contraindicated with MAOIs.

src.q: Carbamazepine is a potent inducer of CYP3A4 and other phase I and phase II enzyme systems in the liver
The use of Tegretol is contraindicated in combination with monoamine-oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs)

items.t: Raise carbamazepine levels (adjust dose and/or monitor levels): macrolides (e.g. clarithromycin), ciprofloxacin, fluoxetine, azole antifungals (e.g. fluconazole, itraconazole), diltiazem, verapamil, possibly omeprazole, isoniazid, danazol, grapefruit juice.

src.q: the dosage of Tegretol should be adjusted accordingly and/or the plasma levels monitored when used concomitantly with the substances described below
Antibiotics: macrolide antibiotics (e.g. erythromycin, clarithromycin), ciprofloxacine. Antidepressants: fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, trazodone.
Antifungals: azoles (e.g. itraconazole, ketoconazole, fluconazole, voriconazole).
Cardiovascular drugs: diltiazem, verapamil. Gastrointestinal drugs: possibly cimetidine, omeprazole. Other interactions: grapefruit juice

items.t: Lower carbamazepine levels: phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone, oxcarbazepine, rifampicin, theophylline, St John's wort. MHRA: advise patients with epilepsy not to use St John's wort.

src.q: Other interactions: herbal preparations containing St John's wort (Hypericum perforatum).
concomitant use of St John's wort and antiepileptic medicine is not recommended

items.t: Carbamazepine lowers levels of (dose may need adjusting): warfarin and DOACs (thrombosis risk), hormonal contraceptives and oestrogen/progestogen products, levothyroxine, corticosteroids (prednisolone, dexamethasone), simvastatin, atorvastatin, dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers, sertraline, tricyclics (e.g. amitriptyline), doxycycline, tramadol, paracetamol, many antiepileptics, antipsychotics and immunosuppressants.

src.q: Carbamazepine may lower the plasma level, diminish or even abolish the activity of certain drugs.
Anticoagulants: oral anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin, acenocoumarol, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, apixaban and edoxaban).
Contraceptives: hormonal contraceptives (alternative contraceptive methods should be considered).
Corticosteroids: corticosteroids (e.g. prednisolone, dexamethasone).
Thyroid agents: levothyroxine.

items.t: Paracetamol long-term with carbamazepine may be associated with hepatotoxicity.

src.q: long term administration of carbamazepine and paracetamol (acetaminophen) may be associated with hepatotoxicity

items.t: Diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide, furosemide): may cause symptomatic hyponatraemia. Lithium: enhanced neurotoxicity. Metoclopramide or major tranquillisers: more neurological side effects. Alcohol: reduced tolerance, advise abstaining.

src.q: Concomitant medication with Tegretol and some diuretics (hydrochlorothiazide, furosemide) may lead to symptomatic hyponatraemia.
The combination of lithium and carbamazepine may cause enhanced neurotoxicity in spite of lithium plasma concentrations being within the therapeutic range.
Combined use of carbamazepine with metoclopramide or major tranquillisers, e.g. haloperidol, thioridazine, may also result in an increase in neurological side-effects.
It is therefore advisable for the patient to abstain from alcohol.

items.t: Direct oral anticoagulants (rivaroxaban, dabigatran, apixaban, edoxaban): reduced levels with thrombosis risk; if needed, monitor closely for thrombosis.

src.q: if a concomitant use is necessary, closer monitoring of signs and symptoms of thrombosis is recommended

items.t: SmPC: increased risk of major malformations after first-trimester exposure (about 4.93% vs 2 to 3% background: neural tube defects, cleft lip/palate, cardiac, hypospadias); neurodevelopmental risk cannot be excluded.
